title: Name the span: what one wrong answer should leave behind
brief: An answer was wrong and nobody can say why. Decide what each model call, tool call and agent run must record so that one trace explains it, and how much to trust the standard that names those records. The dials are not given.

blocks.text: A green request can still be a wrong answer

blocks.md: A classic service fails loudly: a 500, a timeout, an exception. An LLM system fails quietly. The request returns 200, the text is fluent and the content is wrong, so error rates stay flat while quality falls. Cost scales with tokens, latency depends on how many model and tool calls the run made, and the evidence you need (the prompt, the retrieved text, the tool result) is also the data you must protect. Observability for these systems therefore records the shape of every run (spans, tokens, finish reasons, tool calls) and treats content as a separate, governed decision (topic w15-t01).

blocks.title: One agent run as a span tree
blocks.alt: An invoke_agent span has two chat spans and an execute_tool span as children. The execute_tool span has a child span created by the MCP server.

flowchart TB

  A --> T[execute_tool search_docs]

  A --> C2[chat model-a again]
blocks.caption: Illustrative shape. The server span joins this trace only if context crossed the hop, which is the subject of level w15-l3. Topic w15-t03.
Span names and what to record (status Development, checked 2026-10-13)
head: Operation
Span name and kind
Record at least
rows: `{gen_ai.operation.name} {gen_ai.request.model}`, kind CLIENT (INTERNAL allowed for in-process models) [[r2]]
Required `gen_ai.operation.name` and `gen_ai.provider.name`. Also `error.type`, `gen_ai.response.finish_reasons` and the `gen_ai.usage.*` token counts
`invoke_agent {gen_ai.agent.name}`. CLIENT for remote agent services, INTERNAL for in-process frameworks [[r3]]
`invoke_workflow {gen_ai.workflow.name}`, INTERNAL, for graphs or orchestrators that coordinate several agents [[r3]]
Agent Framework's own spans are `workflow.build`, `workflow.run` (Python) or `workflow.session` (.NET, Go), `executor.process {executor_id}`, `edge_group.process`, `message.send` [[r11]]
Tool name and duration. Arguments and results are content, so they are opt-in (level w15-l2)

blocks.md: Agent Framework's built-in telemetry follows these names: `invoke_agent <agent_name>` at the top, `chat <model_name>` per model call and `execute_tool <function_name>` per tool. It also emits the metrics `gen_ai.client.operation.duration`, `gen_ai.client.token.usage` and `agent_framework.function.invocation.duration` [[r10]]. Topic w15-t09 covers switching it on.

blocks.title: How firm is the standard? Checked 2026-10-13
blocks.md: Every GenAI convention (inference, agents, events, metrics, MCP) has status **Development**. The docs moved from `open-telemetry/semantic-conventions` to `open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai` (PR 3696, merged 2026-05-05). Release v1.41.1 (2026-05-11) of the old repo still holds the full text, v1.42.0 (2026-06-12) holds only a Moved stub, and the opentelemetry.io page shows Moved. The new repo has no tagged release, so pin by commit. Agent Framework docs still link the old URL [[r1]].

blocks.title: Failure modes of the first dashboard

items.symptom: The answer was wrong, yet every span is green and the error rate is flat.
items.cause: Semantic failures raise no exception. The trace has no finish reasons, tool results or quality scores to expose them.
items.fix: Record `gen_ai.response.finish_reasons`, tool call counts and an online quality score as attributes or linked evaluation results, and look at long or odd runs by token count.

items.symptom: A token panel built on `gen_ai.client.token.usage` goes blank after instrumentation is upgraded.
items.cause: The v1.41 docs defined that histogram. The new repo defines usage counters named `gen_ai.client.inference.usage.*`, while Agent Framework docs still list the older name [[r5]].
items.fix: Check which names your build and your backend actually emit, and pin the conventions version before building dashboards.

items.symptom: A .NET service emits no `gen_ai.*` spans at all.
items.cause: Spans appear only after the chat client or agent is wrapped with `UseOpenTelemetry`. The Harness wraps both layers by default, a plain agent does not [[r10]].
items.fix: Wrap one layer (not both), call `AddSource` with the same source name on the tracer and meter providers, and confirm with a one-hour query.

quiz.q: Match each operation to its span name pattern.

pairs.l: A tool call in Agent Framework

quiz.explain: The inference span carries the operation (for example chat) and the model. Agent and workflow spans carry the agent or workflow name. Agent Framework names tool spans after the function it runs.

quiz.q: A token panel built on the histogram `gen_ai.client.token.usage` goes blank after the team upgrades its instrumentation to follow the current conventions. Spans still look fine. What is the most likely cause?
options: Spans are sampled, so metrics derived from them are sampled and sometimes empty
The conventions have Development status: the v1.41 histogram was replaced in the new repo by usage counters `gen_ai.client.inference.usage.*`
Content capture is off, so token metrics are not emitted
Token metrics exist only for agents that call at least one tool
quiz.explain: Names moved between the v1.41 docs and the new repo, which is what Development status allows. Metrics are not derived from sampled spans, content capture does not gate token metrics, and token usage is recorded for plain model calls too.

quiz.q: Which statement about the OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions is accurate on 2026-10-13?
options: They are stable, so you can build dashboards on attribute names without pinning anything
They live at opentelemetry.io under `/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/` with versioned releases
They moved to `semantic-conventions-genai` on 2026-05-05, and since that repo has no tags the practical pin is a commit
The old repo's v1.42.0 still holds the full GenAI text
quiz.explain: Status is Development. The page on opentelemetry.io shows Moved, the new repo has no tagged release, and v1.42.0 of the old repo holds only a stub, while v1.41.1 (2026-05-11) holds the last full text.

takeaways: An LLM failure is a fluent 200, so record the shape of the run (spans, tokens, finish reasons, tool calls) and treat content as a separate decision.
Know the names: model calls, `invoke_agent`, `execute_tool` and `invoke_workflow` (Agent Framework also has its own workflow spans).
Every GenAI convention is in Development and moved repositories on 2026-05-05, so pin by commit and check which metric names your build emits.
In .NET, `gen_ai.*` spans exist only after you wrap the client or the agent, and wrapping both duplicates content.
